gasModel.note: Planning only, keyed by fee schedule: never apply one schedule's constants on a chain running the other. gas(publication) = fixed + Σ actions; a new PUBLISH costs publishNew[type] + perWord × ceil(bodyBytes / 32) + perByte × bodyBytes. Excludes the 21,000 intrinsic cost and calldata, which the caller adds from the encoded transaction. eth_estimateGas on the exact call stays the authority before sending.

prague.status: mainnet and Sepolia today (Fusaka); the cap counts all gas

floor.formula: The kernel's quote (LedgerIngress._foldAndQuote, work-model formula 3, docs/WORK-MODEL-V3.md) over a publication of n actions: fresh10 = workModel.freshPerPublication + Σ over PUBLISH/REUSE (freshPerRef·types[T].refs, plus freshPerPublishFresh + freshPerDigestSpec·types[T].specs when the record is new, or freshPerPublishExisting when it exists: a repeat PUBLISH or any REUSE) + Σ over rows (fresh); rw10 = rwPerPublication + rwPerPublish per PUBLISH/REUSE + Σ over rows (rw); compute = computeBase + n·computePerAction + Σ over rows (compute). Each BIND/UNBIND/RELEASE adds one row by class: (freshPerBindFirst, rwPerBindFirst, computePerBindFirst) for a first statement (a BIND or UNBIND whose author's head at the position is UNSET), (freshPerRebind, rwPerRebind, computePerRebind) for a re-bind (a BIND on a BOUND head: a new target, or the same target with a new number), and (freshPerBindLater, rwPerBindLater, computePerBindLater) for every other later statement (a mask, a release, a restore; a RELEASE always); when its purpose word equals surchargePurpose (plain equality, as the kernel compares them; a statement's purpose is never zero, so a zero surchargePurpose surcharges nothing) the surcharge row of the same class is added too (surchargeFreshFirst, surchargeRwFirst, surchargeComputeFirst; surchargeFreshRebind, surchargeRwRebind, surchargeComputeRebind; surchargeFreshLater, surchargeRwLater, surchargeComputeLater). Every WITHDRAW after the first of a publication adds the later-statement row (without the surcharge). With no principal (indexFloor) every bind-kind action adds the largest of the three rows field by field, surcharge included. freshSlots = ceil(fresh10 / 10), rewrites = ceil(rw10 / 10). The kernel refuses a work model whose reply is not 32 words or whose formulaVersion is not 3 (E_WORK_MODEL). prefixFloor P = compute + freshSlots·limits.floorFreshGas + rewrites·limits.floorRewriteGas; finalReserve F = finalComputeBase + binds·finalComputePerBind + publishes·finalComputePerPublish (binds = the BIND/UNBIND/RELEASE count, publishes = the PUBLISH/REUSE count). The checks (design §6.4, §6.5): before callback i the kernel requires its gasleft g > F + T and forwards (g − F − T)·63/64 to the ingress, which spends at most dispatchOverhead, then requires (its gasleft)·63/64 ≥ R_i = max(0, P − the callbacks' spend so far) (E_INDEX_GAS otherwise); before the final phase it requires (g − T)·63/64 ≥ F. T = limits.kernelTail. Sufficient visible execution gas (G = the gas limit less intrinsic gas and calldata; E and K as measured carry the intrinsic cost and the calldata too, the model's note, so the condition is conservative by that much): G ≥ V = max(K + ceil((ceil(P·64/63) + dispatchOverhead)·64/63), E) + ceil(F·64/63) + T, where E is the publication's execution gas and K the kernel's own share of it (callbacks excluded): at callback i the gas spent so far is at most K plus the callbacks' spend s, and R_i·(64/63)² ≥ P·(64/63)² − s, so the kernel's spend and the floor never need more than K + P·(64/63)²; the final check needs at most E + F·64/63 + T. A planner uses the model's execution estimate for E (prague: constants; amsterdam: split.executionGas) and floor.kernel (the same model fitted with the callbacks removed) for K. ILedgerCommitments.indexFloor quotes without a principal, so it prices every bind-kind action with the largest of the three rows field by field: it is an upper bound on P only, and a consumer plans from this rule, never from indexFloor.
floor.quantity: execution gas visible to the GAS opcode (on amsterdam the EIP-8037 state-gas reservoir is not visible and the cap counts execution gas only)

amsterdam.status: EIP-8037/8038 (Glamsterdam); the cap counts execution gas only, and the total must also fit the block

planning.rule: A publication is planned when it is inside limits (1 ≤ actions ≤ maxActions, bind-kind actions ≤ maxBindsPerPublication, PUBLISH body bytes ≤ maxBodyBytesPerPublication) and max(E, V) ≤ floor(txGasCap × (100 − headroomPercent) / 100), on the schedule of the chain: E the model's execution estimate (prague: constants; amsterdam: split.executionGas), V the floor's visible-gas requirement (profiles.<schedule>.floor.formula). A guarded publication is also inside the read-set limits (principals ≤ maxReadSetPrincipals, positions ≤ maxReadSetPositions, principals × positions ≤ maxReadCount) and its E and K carry profiles.<schedule>.guard once. A shape that does not fit is split into publications before it is signed, never shortened; eth_estimateGas on the exact call stays the authority before sending, and the gas limit comes from the estimate, never from V.
planning.txGasCapRule: EIP-7825 (on amsterdam, EIP-8037: the cap counts execution gas only)
planning.headroomCovers: the model's own error over the validation composites (the 21,000 intrinsic cost and the calldata are inside E, K and V: the model's note; earlier releases listed them here) in both states (the author's lists new and existing). The cap condition is tested against the under-prediction of the gas the cap counts (headroom exists to stop a plan coming out too small; an over-prediction only costs batch size): on prague all gas, profiles.prague.maxUnderErrorPercent; on amsterdam execution gas only, profiles.amsterdam.maxUnderExecutionErrorPercent. The maximum-error fields keep their meaning (maxAbsErrorPercent, and on amsterdam maxAbsExecutionErrorPercent); profiles.amsterdam.maxAbsErrorPercent is the all-gas error (execution + state gas), which bounds the publication's total against the block, never the 2^24 cap. Each figure names its composite (maxAbsErrorComposite, maxUnderErrorComposite, maxAbsExecutionErrorComposite, maxUnderExecutionErrorComposite), each is taken over the composites whose state is not in maximaExcludeStates. The under-prediction fields and the over-prediction of the gas the cap counts (profiles.prague.maxOverErrorPercent, profiles.amsterdam.maxOverExecutionErrorPercent) are at most headroomPercent; profiles.amsterdam.maxOverErrorPercent (all gas) is stated with a per-composite bound (method.maxima)

tagLists.note: A per-author (scope-below) or shared (place-below) roll-up list holding exactly one entry, or a multiple of five entries (zero included: an empty list), takes a fresh word on its next append, so price that append as new (tagLevel.mineNew or sharedNew); otherwise as existing. The fresh word costs one slot rewrite more than a new list, inside the headroom; not separately measured.

envelope.what: how many of one shape fit one atomic publication: the smallest of the gas budget and the Realm limits maxActions and maxBodyBytesPerPublication. For user-facing messages; plan with the constants.
envelope.budgetRule: floor(txGasCap × (100 − headroomPercent) / 100) − fixed, on the gas the cap counts

editSmall.what: edit a file: PUBLISH files-child/1 form 0 with 100 bytes of content, rebind HEAD

edit1k.what: the same with 1,024 bytes of content

createSmall.what: create a file: CREATE, PUBLISH files-root/1 form 0 with 100 bytes, PUBLISH a 12-byte name, BIND HEAD, BIND FOLDER

create1k.what: the same with 1,024 bytes of content

chunk.what: PUBLISH one 8,192-byte files-bytes/1 chunk (8,160 file bytes)
